title: The Oath on the Terrace

steps.text: Three years ago, Justin and I put everything into this tavern.
Eleven silver. Let me count that again.
The elf needs it more than I do.
You tipped him. You never count what leaves your hand.
I bought your loan last spring. Your interest comes to me.
Opening night, you lit the fire. Sober as a judge.
Ruby lit it. I was the one holding the match.
You still tell it that way, don't you?
I saw Justin sign a blood oath. Ask him what he remembers.
I want that debt gone before anyone learns what I signed.
Tonight. Before the wrong person reads my name.
If tonight passes unpaid, the council takes the tavern.
Every bottle, every chair, and whoever signed for it.
The savings jar covers her. Barely.
Or Ruby never learns about the oath, and I lie to her.

choice.say: Candy, you'll have the savings jar. Tonight.

then.text: Good. I'll count it myself, then.
Three years of tips, gone in one count.

choice.say: Keep the savings out of this. Give me time.

then.text: Keep your secret, then. I'll still collect.
She's smiling. That's never good news.

steps.text: Not the savings, Justin. That's our tavern, not your debt.
Boots on the stairs. Slow. Someone reading a list.
My name is on that list. I know it before he speaks.

choice.say: Not tonight. I'm going out the back.

then.text: Go on, run. Leave me with the bill, like always.
Then I'll collect from whoever's left.

choice.say: I'm here. Read your list, then.

then.text: Then take it alone. I won't pay for your oath.
Her footsteps go down the stairs. Mine stay.

next: If he paid from the savings, Ruby finds the jar empty and asks why.
If he hid the oath, Candy uses his silence to squeeze more interest from him.
If he stayed, the runner's list names him in front of Ruby.
If he ran, he has one night to find the money before the council does.
